Split `gw3/gateway.go`'s single 60-line closure — which mixed path classification, method checking, and three unrelated response bodies (health, list, get-by-one) at one indent level — into a small `accountsHandler` type with one method per route. ## Changes

| Location | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| anonymous `http.HandlerFunc` closure | routing, method check, and 3 response bodies inline in one function | `accountsHandler.ServeHTTP` dispatching via `switch` to `serveHealthz`/`serveList`/`serveGet` | each route is now readable on its own; mixed abstraction levels (string parsing, query validation, domain filtering) no longer share one indent level |
| `"/healthz"`, `"/accounts"`, `"/accounts/"`, `"active"` literals | repeated string literals | `healthzPath`, `accountsPath`, `accountsPrefix`, `activeParamName` constants | names the magic values once (Playbook §4) |
| two identical `http.Error(w, \`invalid query parameter "active"\`, 400)` calls | duplicated inline | `writeInvalidActiveParam(w)` | same literal error text, same status, appeared twice verbatim |
| `strings.HasPrefix` + slicing | three-clause boolean | `isAccountPath` via `strings.CutPrefix` | equivalent (`CutPrefix` returns the same suffix and `ok`), reads as one intent |

Net line growth (+28) comes entirely from named function boundaries and constants for a handler whose readability problem was structural (multiple unrelated branches at one nesting level), not from added logic — no new behavior, no new dependency.

## Modernization

`strings.HasPrefix(path, prefix) && ...slicing` → `strings.CutPrefix`. Equivalent per BEHAVIOR-TRAPS.md's modernization table entry for that swap; no other Tier-1/2 items applied.

## Behavior risk

The one place this could have silently changed the wire format: the "list all, no `active` filter" branch. The original always builds `filtered := make([]Account, 0, len(accounts))` then appends into it, so an empty account list serializes as `[]`, never `null`, even when the input slice was nil. I preserved that exact construction (`writeJSON(w, append(filtered, h.accounts...))`) instead of writing `h.accounts` directly, which would have sent `null` for a nil input.
